# Flag reference

<!-- Generated by tools/flagdoc from cmd/remotesigner/flags. Do not edit; run `make docs`. -->

```
remotesigner [global flags] consensus [consensus flags]
remotesigner [global flags] consensus [consensus flags] migrate [migrate flags]
remotesigner [global flags] consensus [consensus flags] randao-state reset --key <id> [reset flags]
remotesigner [global flags] consensus [consensus flags] import --from <file> [import flags]
remotesigner [global flags] consensus [consensus flags] export --to <file> [--keys <id>,...] [export flags]
remotesigner [global flags] consensus [consensus flags] watermark-repair --epoch <epoch> --slot <slot> [repair flags]
remotesigner [global flags] consensus [consensus flags] set-high-watermark (--epoch <epoch> --slot <slot> | --remove) [flags]
remotesigner [global flags] consensus [consensus flags] disable-validator --key <id> [flags]
remotesigner [global flags] consensus keystore verify --file <keystore> --password-file <file>
remotesigner [global flags] consensus keystore verify --keystores-path <dir> (--keystores-password-file <file> | --keystores-passwords-path <dir>)
remotesigner [global flags] execution [execution flags]
remotesigner --version
```

`execution` exists only in the default flavour, `remotesigner`; `remotesigner-consensus` has no such command
and refuses an `execution:` section in its config file.

Every global, consensus and execution flag can also be set (the subcommands' own flags read what their tables list):

- in the environment, as `REMOTESIGNER_<NAME>` for a global flag, `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_<NAME>` for a
  consensus flag and `REMOTESIGNER_EXECUTION_<NAME>` for an execution flag (the flag name or any alias in upper
  case, dashes as underscores);
- in the YAML file given by `--config-file`, under its bare name or any of its aliases (the Config file column lists
  them all). Consensus and execution flags may sit at the top level or in a `consensus:` or `execution:`
  section. A list flag takes a YAML list. Unknown keys are rejected, and so is a flag set under two of its names.

Precedence: command line, then environment, then config file, then default. Booleans are written `--flag`,
`--flag=true` or `--flag=false`. `--flag false` does not work: the command-line parser (urfave/cli) reads
`false` as an argument, which every command refuses as a usage error, so write `=` where Web3Signer takes the
value as the next argument (`--slashing-protection-enabled=false`). In the environment and the config file a
boolean takes a value, such as `true` or `false`. Exit codes: 2 for usage errors (including a missing `--network` and an
invalid config file), 1 when the signer refuses to start or fails.

Signals: `SIGHUP` re-reads the token files, the TLS certificate and the client trust files
([`../operations/tls.md`](../operations/tls.md#5-rotating-tokens-and-certificates-with-sighup)); key files are
reloaded with `POST /reload` instead ([`../operations/reload.md`](../operations/reload.md#3-reload)).
`SIGTERM` and `SIGINT` stop the signer: it stops accepting connections, lets in-flight requests finish for
up to 10 s, closes the store, wipes the keys and exits 0.

## Global flags

| Flag | Environment | Config file | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--config-file` | none | none | unset | YAML file of flag values: bare flag names, with an optional consensus: section. Unknown keys are rejected. |
| `--data-path` | `REMOTESIGNER_DATA_PATH` | `data-path` | unset | Directory for the generated token files, the slashing-protection store and the ports file |
| `--key-config-path`, `--key-store-path` | `REMOTESIGNER_KEY_CONFIG_PATH`, `REMOTESIGNER_KEY_STORE_PATH` | `key-config-path` or `key-store-path` | unset | Directory of key-config files (\*.yaml or \*.yml; types file-raw, file-keystore, hashicorp, aws-secret, azure-secret and gcp-secret); unset loads none |
| `--key-store-config-file-max-size` | `REMOTESIGNER_KEY_STORE_CONFIG_FILE_MAX_SIZE` | `key-store-config-file-max-size` | `104857600` | Largest key-config file loaded, in bytes (Web3Signer counts code points); a larger file fails to load. Must be above 0. |
| `--strict-file-permissions` | `REMOTESIGNER_STRICT_FILE_PERMISSIONS` | `strict-file-permissions` | `true` | Refuse secret files (password files, key-config files with a seed or a secret-store credential, the token files, and the TLS private key, keystore and keystore password file) that their group or other users can read, and, with --key-manager-api-enabled, a --key-config-path directory they can access; false loads them with a warning |
| `--reload-timeout` | `REMOTESIGNER_RELOAD_TIMEOUT` | `reload-timeout` | `60` | Minutes a POST /reload may load keys; the sources not loaded by then keep their previous keys. The startup load is not bounded. |
| `--signer-load-parallelism` | `REMOTESIGNER_SIGNER_LOAD_PARALLELISM` | `signer-load-parallelism` | `0 (from the memory limit)` | Keystore decrypts with the standard KDF that may run at once; 0 sizes the Argon2id budget from GOMEMLIMIT, the cgroup limit or half the RAM |
| `--logging`, `-l` | `REMOTESIGNER_LOGGING`, `REMOTESIGNER_L` | `logging` or `l` | `INFO` | Log level: OFF, FATAL, ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG, TRACE or ALL |
| `--logging-format`, `--log-format` | `REMOTESIGNER_LOGGING_FORMAT`, `REMOTESIGNER_LOG_FORMAT` | `logging-format` or `log-format` | `text` | Log format: text or json |
| `--log-file` | `REMOTESIGNER_LOG_FILE` | `log-file` | unset | Write logs to this file instead of standard error |
| `--http-listen-host` | `REMOTESIGNER_HTTP_LISTEN_HOST` | `http-listen-host` | `127.0.0.1` | Host the API listens on. A non-loopback host turns on the remote-listener fail-safes. |
| `--http-listen-port` | `REMOTESIGNER_HTTP_LISTEN_PORT` | `http-listen-port` | `9000` | Port the API listens on; 0 picks a free port (see the ports file) |
| `--http-host-allowlist` | `REMOTESIGNER_HTTP_HOST_ALLOWLIST` | `http-host-allowlist` | `localhost,127.0.0.1,::1` | Host header names the API accepts (DNS-rebinding defence); \* or all accepts any, none refuses all |
| `--http-auth-mode` | `REMOTESIGNER_HTTP_AUTH_MODE` | `http-auth-mode` | `token` | API authentication: token (the sign token), mtls (a client certificate grants the sign scope), token+mtls (both) or none (loopback listeners only). Admin routes always need the admin token. |
| `--http-auth-token-file` | `REMOTESIGNER_HTTP_AUTH_TOKEN_FILE` | `http-auth-token-file` | unset | Sign-scope bearer token file (default \<data-path>/auth-token, generated 0600 when missing; re-read on SIGHUP) |
| `--http-admin-token-file` | `REMOTESIGNER_HTTP_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE` | `http-admin-token-file` | unset | Admin-scope bearer token file (default \<data-path>/admin-token, generated 0600 when missing; re-read on SIGHUP). Admin routes exist only with an admin token. |
| `--http-max-connections` | `REMOTESIGNER_HTTP_MAX_CONNECTIONS` | `http-max-connections` | `1024` | Maximum open API connections; further connections wait until one closes |
| `--idle-connection-timeout-seconds` | `REMOTESIGNER_IDLE_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `idle-connection-timeout-seconds` | `120` | Seconds a kept-alive API connection may stay idle |
| `--max-concurrent-signing-requests` | `REMOTESIGNER_MAX_CONCURRENT_SIGNING_REQUESTS` | `max-concurrent-signing-requests` | `32` | Sign requests that may be in their slashing check, signature and verification at once; the others wait in the queue (replaces Web3Signer's --vertx-worker-pool-size). Must be at least 1. |
| `--max-queued-signing-requests` | `REMOTESIGNER_MAX_QUEUED_SIGNING_REQUESTS` | `max-queued-signing-requests` | `512` | Sign requests that may wait for --max-concurrent-signing-requests; one more is refused at once with 503 OVERLOADED and Retry-After. 0 queues none. |
| `--access-logs-enabled` | `REMOTESIGNER_ACCESS_LOGS_ENABLED` | `access-logs-enabled` | `false` | Log every API request at INFO (route, status, duration; never paths or bodies) |
| `--tls-cert-file` | `REMOTESIGNER_TLS_CERT_FILE` | `tls-cert-file` | unset | PEM certificate chain the API serves over TLS 1.3, with --tls-key-file (re-read on SIGHUP) |
| `--tls-key-file` | `REMOTESIGNER_TLS_KEY_FILE` | `tls-key-file` | unset | PEM private key of --tls-cert-file |
| `--tls-keystore-file` | `REMOTESIGNER_TLS_KEYSTORE_FILE` | `tls-keystore-file` | unset | PKCS#12 keystore with the API's TLS key and certificate chain, instead of PEM; with --tls-keystore-password-file (re-read on SIGHUP) |
| `--tls-keystore-password-file` | `REMOTESIGNER_TLS_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD_FILE` | `tls-keystore-password-file` | unset | File whose first line is the password of --tls-keystore-file |
| `--tls-generate-self-signed` | `REMOTESIGNER_TLS_GENERATE_SELF_SIGNED` | `tls-generate-self-signed` | `false` | Serve TLS with a self-signed ECDSA P-256 certificate, generated 0600 into \<data-path>/tls/ on first start for the --http-host-allowlist names and reused after; a configured certificate takes precedence |
| `--tls-known-clients-file` | `REMOTESIGNER_TLS_KNOWN_CLIENTS_FILE` | `tls-known-clients-file` | unset | Client certificates the mtls modes accept: lines of "\<label> \<SHA-256 fingerprint>" (Web3Signer's format; re-read on SIGHUP) |
| `--tls-client-ca-file` | `REMOTESIGNER_TLS_CLIENT_CA_FILE` | `tls-client-ca-file` | unset | PEM CAs whose client certificates the mtls modes accept; the system roots are never used (re-read on SIGHUP) |
| `--metrics-enabled` | `REMOTESIGNER_METRICS_ENABLED` | `metrics-enabled` | `false` | Serve Prometheus metrics at /metrics on a separate listener |
| `--metrics-host` | `REMOTESIGNER_METRICS_HOST` | `metrics-host` | `127.0.0.1` | Host the metrics listener binds |
| `--metrics-port` | `REMOTESIGNER_METRICS_PORT` | `metrics-port` | `9001` | Port the metrics listener binds; 0 picks a free port (see the ports file) |
| `--metrics-host-allowlist` | `REMOTESIGNER_METRICS_HOST_ALLOWLIST` | `metrics-host-allowlist` | `localhost,127.0.0.1` | Host header names the metrics listener accepts; \* or all accepts any, none refuses all |
| `--metrics-auth-token-file` | `REMOTESIGNER_METRICS_AUTH_TOKEN_FILE` | `metrics-auth-token-file` | unset | Bearer token file the metrics listener requires (generated 0600 when missing; re-read on SIGHUP); unset leaves /metrics open |
| `--disable-core-dumps` | `REMOTESIGNER_DISABLE_CORE_DUMPS` | `disable-core-dumps` | `true` | On Linux, make the process non-dumpable (no core dumps, no ptrace or /proc memory reads by other processes) and set its core-file limit to 0 |
| `--mlock-all` | `REMOTESIGNER_MLOCK_ALL` | `mlock-all` | `false` | On Linux, lock all process memory so that keys are never swapped out (needs CAP_IPC_LOCK or an unlimited RLIMIT_MEMLOCK; refused otherwise) |

## Consensus flags

| Flag | Environment | Config file | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--network` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_NETWORK` | `network` or `consensus.network` | unset | Required. A built-in network name (minimal, end-to-end or e2e, end-to-end-mainnet, interop) or a qrysm-format config YAML file |
| `--network-genesis-validators-root` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_NETWORK_GENESIS_VALIDATORS_ROOT` | `network-genesis-validators-root` or `consensus.network-genesis-validators-root` | unset | Genesis validators root, 0x + 64 hex characters; must agree with every other source |
| `--network-genesis-time` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_NETWORK_GENESIS_TIME` | `network-genesis-time` or `consensus.network-genesis-time` | unset | Genesis time in Unix seconds; must agree with every other source |
| `--network-genesis-state` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_NETWORK_GENESIS_STATE` | `network-genesis-state` or `consensus.network-genesis-state` | unset | SSZ genesis state; its first 64 bytes give the genesis time, the genesis validators root and the fork |
| `--slashing-protection-enabled` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_SLASHING_PROTECTION_ENABLED` | `slashing-protection-enabled` or `consensus.slashing-protection-enabled` | `true` | Slashing protection, in the store --slashing-protection-db-url names (default the bbolt file \<data-path>/slashing-protection.db). false is allowed only when every listener is loopback. |
| `--key-manager-api-enabled`, `--enable-key-manager-api` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_KEY_MANAGER_API_ENABLED`, `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_ENABLE_KEY_MANAGER_API` | `key-manager-api-enabled`, `enable-key-manager-api`, `consensus.key-manager-api-enabled` or `consensus.enable-key-manager-api` | `false` | Serve the keymanager API (GET, POST and DELETE /qrl/v1/keystores) with the admin token; imported keys are written to --key-config-path, which it requires (docs/operations/keymanager.md). |
| `--voluntary-exit-signing-enabled` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_VOLUNTARY_EXIT_SIGNING_ENABLED` | `voluntary-exit-signing-enabled` or `consensus.voluntary-exit-signing-enabled` | `false` | Sign VOLUNTARY_EXIT requests; refused with 403 ARTIFACT_TYPE_DISABLED otherwise |
| `--registration-fee-recipient-file` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_REGISTRATION_FEE_RECIPIENT_FILE` | `registration-fee-recipient-file` or `consensus.registration-fee-recipient-file` | unset | YAML list of {key, fee_recipient} pins: a VALIDATOR_REGISTRATION for a pinned key must carry its pinned fee recipient |
| `--signing-clock-skew-slots` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_SIGNING_CLOCK_SKEW_SLOTS` | `signing-clock-skew-slots` or `consensus.signing-clock-skew-slots` | `1` | Slots a slot-scoped request may lie ahead of the wall clock (when genesis time is known) |
| `--selection-proof-signing` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_SELECTION_PROOF_SIGNING` | `selection-proof-signing` or `consensus.selection-proof-signing` | `deterministic` | Signing mode of AGGREGATION_SLOT and SYNC_COMMITTEE_SELECTION_PROOF: deterministic or hedged; other types are always hedged |
| `--slashing-protection-db-url` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_SLASHING_PROTECTION_DB_URL` | `slashing-protection-db-url` or `consensus.slashing-protection-db-url` | unset | Slashing-protection store: bolt:///absolute/path/file.db (default \<data-path>/slashing-protection.db), or a Postgres database as postgres://user@host:port/database?sslmode=verify-full (jdbc:postgresql:// is accepted) without a password, migrated with consensus migrate |
| `--slashing-protection-db-username` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_SLASHING_PROTECTION_DB_USERNAME` | `slashing-protection-db-username` or `consensus.slashing-protection-db-username` | unset | User name for the Postgres store, instead of the URL's |
| `--slashing-protection-db-password-file` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_SLASHING_PROTECTION_DB_PASSWORD_FILE` | `slashing-protection-db-password-file` or `consensus.slashing-protection-db-password-file` | unset | File whose first line is the Postgres store's password (owner-readable only, like other secret files); without it the password comes from PGPASSFILE (default ~/.pgpass), under the same rule. PGPASSWORD, a password in the URL and one in a pg_service.conf service are refused. |
| `--slashing-protection-db-health-check-timeout-milliseconds` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_SLASHING_PROTECTION_DB_HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MILLISECONDS` | `slashing-protection-db-health-check-timeout-milliseconds` or `consensus.slashing-protection-db-health-check-timeout-milliseconds` | `3000` | Milliseconds after which the Postgres store's health check fails (slashing-protection-db-health-check) |
| `--slashing-protection-db-health-check-interval-milliseconds` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_SLASHING_PROTECTION_DB_HEALTH_CHECK_INTERVAL_MILLISECONDS` | `slashing-protection-db-health-check-interval-milliseconds` or `consensus.slashing-protection-db-health-check-interval-milliseconds` | `30000` | Milliseconds between two health checks of the Postgres store; /healthcheck reports the last one |
| `--slashing-protection-db-migrate` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_SLASHING_PROTECTION_DB_MIGRATE` | `slashing-protection-db-migrate` or `consensus.slashing-protection-db-migrate` | `false` | Upgrade an older slashing-protection store to this release's schema before starting: a bbolt file is backed up to \<file>.v\<old>.bak first; a Postgres database without the schema gets it, which needs a role that may create tables |
| `--slashing-protection-pruning-epochs-to-keep` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_SLASHING_PROTECTION_PRUNING_EPOCHS_TO_KEEP` | `slashing-protection-pruning-epochs-to-keep` or `consensus.slashing-protection-pruning-epochs-to-keep` | `512` | Epochs of block and attestation history each validator keeps below its newest record (slots per epoch come from the network); older records are pruned |
| `--slashing-protection-pruning-interval` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_SLASHING_PROTECTION_PRUNING_INTERVAL` | `slashing-protection-pruning-interval` or `consensus.slashing-protection-pruning-interval` | `12h0m0s` | Time between two slashing-protection pruning runs, as a duration such as 12h or 90m (Web3Signer's bare number of hours is refused); with bbolt the first runs at startup, with Postgres one interval after it |
| `--randao-max-layers` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_RANDAO_MAX_LAYERS` | `randao-max-layers` or `consensus.randao-max-layers` | `1048576` | Onion layers searched from x_0 when locating a RANDAO commitment; a commitment deeper in a longer onion is unknown |
| `--randao-reorg-window` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_RANDAO_REORG_WINDOW` | `randao-reorg-window` or `consensus.randao-reorg-window` | `1024` | Layers above a key's released frontier searched for a re-reveal before the slow-path scan |
| `--randao-full-scan-min-interval` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_RANDAO_FULL_SCAN_MIN_INTERVAL` | `randao-full-scan-min-interval` or `consensus.randao-full-scan-min-interval` | `SECONDS_PER_SLOT` | Minimum time between two slow-path RANDAO scans of one key (first use, gap advance, deep reorg); sooner gets 429 RANDAO_SCAN_RATE_LIMITED |
| `--randao-new-layer-burst` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_RANDAO_NEW_LAYER_BURST` | `randao-new-layer-burst` or `consensus.randao-new-layer-burst` | `3` | Tokens in each key's RANDAO new-layer bucket: frontier-moving reveals allowed in a burst |
| `--randao-new-layer-refill-epochs` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_RANDAO_NEW_LAYER_REFILL_EPOCHS` | `randao-new-layer-refill-epochs` or `consensus.randao-new-layer-refill-epochs` | `1` | Epochs per new-layer token refill; 0 turns the bucket off. Networks with fewer than about 4 x SLOTS_PER_EPOCH validators should raise the burst or use 0. |
| `--randao-protection-required` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_RANDAO_PROTECTION_REQUIRED` | `randao-protection-required` or `consensus.randao-protection-required` | `false` | Refuse to start when RANDAO frontiers would be kept in memory only (--slashing-protection-enabled=false) |
| `--keystores-path` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_KEYSTORES_PATH` | `keystores-path` or `consensus.keystores-path` | unset | Directory of keystores to load: every non-hidden \*.json file in it (deposit CLI or qrysm keystore v1) |
| `--keystores-password-file` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_KEYSTORES_PASSWORD_FILE` | `keystores-password-file` or `consensus.keystores-password-file` | unset | File holding the password of every keystore in --keystores-path; not with --keystores-passwords-path |
| `--keystores-passwords-path` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_KEYSTORES_PASSWORDS_PATH` | `keystores-passwords-path` or `consensus.keystores-passwords-path` | unset | Directory of password files, \<name>.txt for keystore \<name>.json; not with --keystores-password-file |
| `--aws-secrets-enabled` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_AWS_SECRETS_ENABLED` | `aws-secrets-enabled` or `consensus.aws-secrets-enabled` | `false` | Bulk-load seeds from AWS Secrets Manager: every secret the prefix and tag filters select, one 48-byte seed (hex) per line. Default flavour only. |
| `--aws-secrets-auth-mode` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_AWS_SECRETS_AUTH_MODE` | `aws-secrets-auth-mode` or `consensus.aws-secrets-auth-mode` | `SPECIFIED` | AWS authentication of the bulk loader: SPECIFIED (--aws-secrets-access-key-id and --aws-secrets-secret-access-key) or ENVIRONMENT (the SDK's default chain: environment, shared credentials and config files, web identity, ECS and EC2 roles) |
| `--aws-secrets-access-key-id` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_AWS_SECRETS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | `aws-secrets-access-key-id` or `consensus.aws-secrets-access-key-id` | unset | AWS access key id of SPECIFIED authentication |
| `--aws-secrets-secret-access-key` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_AWS_SECRETS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | `aws-secrets-secret-access-key` or `consensus.aws-secrets-secret-access-key` | unset | AWS secret access key of SPECIFIED authentication; prefer the environment variable, which other users cannot read in the process list |
| `--aws-secrets-region` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_AWS_SECRETS_REGION` | `aws-secrets-region` or `consensus.aws-secrets-region` | unset | AWS region of Secrets Manager; required for SPECIFIED authentication, else the SDK's (AWS_REGION, the shared config file) |
| `--aws-endpoint-override` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_AWS_ENDPOINT_OVERRIDE` | `aws-endpoint-override` or `consensus.aws-endpoint-override` | unset | Secrets Manager endpoint URL instead of AWS's, for the bulk loader (a VPC endpoint, LocalStack) |
| `--aws-secrets-prefixes-filter` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_AWS_SECRETS_PREFIXES_FILTER` | `aws-secrets-prefixes-filter` or `consensus.aws-secrets-prefixes-filter` | unset | Load only the secrets whose names start with one of these prefixes (comma-separated) |
| `--aws-secrets-tag` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_AWS_SECRETS_TAG` | `aws-secrets-tag` or `consensus.aws-secrets-tag` | unset | Load only the secrets with these tags: TAG_NAME=TAG_VALUE, repeated or separated by \|; a name given twice keeps its last value; AWS matches any of the names and any of the non-empty values |
| `--aws-connection-cache-size` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_AWS_CONNECTION_CACHE_SIZE` | `aws-connection-cache-size` or `consensus.aws-connection-cache-size` | `1` | AWS Secrets Manager clients kept for aws-secret key-config documents during a load, by credentials and region |
| `--gcp-secrets-enabled` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_GCP_SECRETS_ENABLED` | `gcp-secrets-enabled` or `consensus.gcp-secrets-enabled` | `false` | Bulk-load seeds from GCP Secret Manager: the latest version of every secret of --gcp-project-id that --gcp-secrets-filter selects, one 48-byte seed (hex) per line, with Application Default Credentials. Default flavour only. |
| `--gcp-project-id` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_GCP_PROJECT_ID` | `gcp-project-id` or `consensus.gcp-project-id` | unset | GCP project of the bulk loader's secrets |
| `--gcp-secrets-filter` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_GCP_SECRETS_FILTER` | `gcp-secrets-filter` or `consensus.gcp-secrets-filter` | unset | Secret Manager list filter (https://cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/filtering); empty loads every secret of the project |
| `--azure-vault-enabled` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_AZURE_VAULT_ENABLED` | `azure-vault-enabled` or `consensus.azure-vault-enabled` | `false` | Bulk-load seeds from the Azure Key Vault --azure-vault-name: every secret with the --azure-tags, one 48-byte seed (hex) per line. Default flavour only. |
| `--azure-vault-auth-mode` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_AZURE_VAULT_AUTH_MODE` | `azure-vault-auth-mode` or `consensus.azure-vault-auth-mode` | `CLIENT_SECRET` | Azure authentication: CLIENT_SECRET, USER_ASSIGNED_MANAGED_IDENTITY or SYSTEM_ASSIGNED_MANAGED_IDENTITY |
| `--azure-vault-name` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_AZURE_VAULT_NAME` | `azure-vault-name` or `consensus.azure-vault-name` | unset | Name of the key vault, the subdomain of vault.azure.net |
| `--azure-client-id` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_AZURE_CLIENT_ID` | `azure-client-id` or `consensus.azure-client-id` | unset | Client id of CLIENT_SECRET or USER_ASSIGNED_MANAGED_IDENTITY authentication; optional for SYSTEM_ASSIGNED_MANAGED_IDENTITY |
| `--azure-tenant-id` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_AZURE_TENANT_ID` | `azure-tenant-id` or `consensus.azure-tenant-id` | unset | Microsoft Entra ID tenant of CLIENT_SECRET authentication |
| `--azure-client-secret` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` | `azure-client-secret` or `consensus.azure-client-secret` | unset | Client secret of CLIENT_SECRET authentication; prefer the environment variable, which other users cannot read in the process list |

Applies to every element of a batch; the signer's own methods are never forwarded. |

Execution mode reads the global flags too; `--key-config-path` and `--keystores-path` then hold account keys
(51-byte extended seeds and go-qrl account keystores). See
[`../operations/execution.md`](../operations/execution.md).

## Store commands

These subcommands work on the slashing-protection store. A bbolt store they open while the signer is stopped (bbolt
allows one process per file; they refuse a store that a running signer holds). A Postgres database they use online,
under the advisory locks the signers take, so the signers keep running
([`../operations/postgres.md`](../operations/postgres.md)). They read `--data-path` for the default bbolt store
location. Their flags are not read from the config file; `--slashing-protection-db-url`,
`--slashing-protection-db-username` and `--slashing-protection-db-password-file` may also be given to
`consensus` itself, on the command line, in the environment or in the config file. `import`, `export`
and `set-high-watermark` also read `--network` and its genesis flags from `consensus`, for the
genesis validators root: `import` and `set-high-watermark` bind a store that has none to it, and `export`
names it in the file of such a store. The history commands are described in
[`../operations/migration.md`](../operations/migration.md).

|---|---|---|---|---|

| `--slashing-protection-db-username` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_SLASHING_PROTECTION_DB_USERNAME` | none | unset | User name for the Postgres store, instead of the URL's |

PGPASSWORD, a password in the URL and one in a pg_service.conf service are refused. |

`consensus disable-validator` persists `enabled=false` for a key, which then gets 412

[`../operations/reload.md`](../operations/reload.md#5-disabling-a-validator).

## Keystore commands

`consensus keystore verify` decrypts one keystore with its password file (`--file`, `--password-file`), or a
keystore directory as the signer loads it (`--keystores-path` with `--keystores-password-file` or
`--keystores-passwords-path`), through the signer's keystore decryptor, policy and file-permission rule, and
checks that each keystore's pubkey is the key its seed derives. It prints each key's identifier and exits 0, or
names the refusals and exits 1. It needs no network, store or running signer. Its own flags read no environment
variables, so that a signer's `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_KEYSTORES_*` settings do not apply to it; the global
`--strict-file-permissions` and `--signer-load-parallelism` do. See
[`../operations/keystores.md`](../operations/keystores.md).

### consensus keystore verify

| Flag | Environment | Config file | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--file` | none | none | unset | The keystore to check: qrysm's keystore v1 or a deposit CLI keystore (JSON); with --password-file |
| `--password-file` | none | none | unset | File holding the keystore's password; trailing line breaks are not part of it |
| `--keystores-path` | none | none | unset | Directory of keystores to load: every non-hidden \*.json file in it (deposit CLI or qrysm keystore v1) |
| `--keystores-password-file` | none | none | unset | File holding the password of every keystore in --keystores-path; not with --keystores-passwords-path |
| `--keystores-passwords-path` | none | none | unset | Directory of password files, \<name>.txt for keystore \<name>.json; not with --keystores-password-file |

## Override flags

These flags are hidden from `--help`. They are set like any other flag, on the command line, in the environment
or in the config file. Each `--Xallow-*` flag lifts a startup refusal that protects a listener beyond loopback,
and accepts the risk that refusal guards against; on a loopback listener none of them is needed. None of them can
re-enable a disabled slashing protection on such a listener: that refusal has no override. The container image, its
entrypoint and the examples in `deploy/` set none of them. The `--Xazure-*` and `--Xgcp-*` overrides
point a secret store's client at another endpoint, authority or trust anchor, as Web3Signer's unstable Azure options
do: for sovereign clouds, private endpoints and emulators.

### Global

| Flag | Environment | Config file | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--Xallow-plaintext-token-auth` | `REMOTESIGNER_XALLOW_PLAINTEXT_TOKEN_AUTH` | `Xallow-plaintext-token-auth` | `false` | Allow bearer tokens over plaintext HTTP on a non-loopback listener |

### Consensus

| Flag | Environment | Config file | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--Xallow-unknown-genesis-time` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_XALLOW_UNKNOWN_GENESIS_TIME` | `Xallow-unknown-genesis-time` or `consensus.Xallow-unknown-genesis-time` | `false` | Allow a non-loopback listener without a genesis time (wall-clock bounds off) |
| `--Xallow-gvr-tofu` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_XALLOW_GVR_TOFU` | `Xallow-gvr-tofu` or `consensus.Xallow-gvr-tofu` | `false` | Allow a non-loopback listener to pin the genesis validators root on first use |
| `--Xgcp-endpoint-override` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_XGCP_ENDPOINT_OVERRIDE` | `Xgcp-endpoint-override` or `consensus.Xgcp-endpoint-override` | unset | Secret Manager endpoint host:port instead of Google's; http://host:port is an emulator, reached without TLS and credentials |
| `--Xazure-endpoint-override` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_XAZURE_ENDPOINT_OVERRIDE` | `Xazure-endpoint-override` or `consensus.Xazure-endpoint-override` | unset | Key Vault URL instead of https://\<vault>.vault.azure.net |
| `--Xazure-authority-host-override` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_XAZURE_AUTHORITY_HOST_OVERRIDE` | `Xazure-authority-host-override` or `consensus.Xazure-authority-host-override` | unset | Microsoft Entra ID authority host URL instead of Azure's |
| `--Xazure-trust-certificate-override` | `REMOTESIGNER_CONSENSUS_XAZURE_TRUST_CERTIFICATE_OVERRIDE` | `Xazure-trust-certificate-override` or `consensus.Xazure-trust-certificate-override` | unset | Certificate file (PEM or DER) trusted for the Key Vault and authority connections instead of the system roots |

### What each override accepts

#### `--Xallow-plaintext-token-auth`

- **Refused without it.** A non-loopback API listener with `--http-auth-mode=token` and no TLS (no `--tls-cert-file`, `--tls-keystore-file` or `--tls-generate-self-signed`). The mtls modes always need TLS, and loopback listeners are never refused.
- **The risk it accepts.** Every request carries the sign or admin token in clear: anyone who can read the traffic (the LAN, the host network, another container on the Docker network) can replay it, sign duties with the sign token (slashing protection still applies) and, with the admin token, reload keys, reset RANDAO frontiers and, with `--key-manager-api-enabled`, import and delete keys. Every response can be read as well, signatures and RANDAO reveals included.
- **Instead.** Serve TLS: `--tls-generate-self-signed`, which the container image sets, or `--tls-cert-file` and `--tls-key-file`, and give the validator client the certificate (`--validators-external-signer-tls-ca-file`). Use the override only on a throwaway test network whose keys guard nothing.

#### `--Xallow-unknown-genesis-time`

- **Refused without it.** A non-loopback API listener when no source gives the genesis time: neither a built-in network that knows it, `--network-genesis-time` nor `--network-genesis-state`.
- **The risk it accepts.** Without a genesis time the signer cannot tell the current slot. Its wall-clock bounds are off, so a client with the sign token can have blocks and attestations signed for slots and epochs far in the future: signatures it can broadcast later, and slashing-protection records that refuse the validator's honest attestations until the chain reaches those epochs. New RANDAO layers are refused, so the validators cannot propose, and capabilities reports a null genesis_time, which the qrysm validator client refuses at startup.
- **Instead.** Pass `--network-genesis-time`, or `--network-genesis-state` with the chain's genesis state.

#### `--Xallow-gvr-tofu`

- **Refused without it.** A non-loopback API listener for a file network when no source gives the genesis validators root: neither `--network-genesis-validators-root` nor `--network-genesis-state`. A built-in network never pins on first use: without one of those flags it refuses to start (exit code 1) on any listener, and the override does not change that.
- **The risk it accepts.** The first request that carries the network's fork version pins its genesis validators root into the slashing-protection store for good, and every later request must match it. Networks built from one configuration share their fork version, so the first client to reach the signer decides which chain it signs for. When that is another chain that uses the same keys, the signer signs for that chain from then on and refuses every request for the intended one. Undoing a wrong pin needs a new store.
- **Instead.** Pass `--network-genesis-validators-root`, or `--network-genesis-state` with the chain's genesis state. Trust on first use is meant for a test network on a loopback listener, as the qrysm end-to-end test runs it.

### Listing them

`remotesigner Xhelp`, Web3Signer's hidden help topic, prints the hidden `--X…` flags of every command with their
environment variables, under a notice that they may change between releases without announcement. It is not listed by
`--help`.
